title: Yosta the Tailor of Tzippori
author: Aharon Hyman
attribution: English translation and editorial notes prepared for Joshua Waxman.

paragraphs: Shir HaShirim Rabbah, at the end of chapter 6, relates that he found favor with the king, who told him, “Ask me for something, and I will give it to you.” He asked to be appointed duke over the city. When he had risen to this office and passed through the city, people were unsure whether he was Yosta the tailor. They said, “Let us use a test: if he looks at his old place when he passes it, that will show that he is Yosta the tailor.” So it was. He told them, “You are amazed at me; I am even more amazed at myself,” etc.[^1]

notes.text: חייטא means tailor. The requested appointment concerns Yosta himself, as the following כשנתעלה לשררה זו confirms; the earlier draft incorrectly had him appointing another duke. מושבו הישן is his old place or seat, without inventing a specific house or workshop. דוכס is retained as duke without fixing a precise administrative rank. שהש״ר ספ״ו conventionally gives Shir HaShirim Rabbah, end of chapter 6; no modern subparagraph is assigned. Hyman ends his abridged story with etc. No named witness was checked.
